intro.title2: From inversion to the final file.
intro.body: A density-domain inversion engine, a full set of color tools, and an automated path through capture, scanning, development, and output. Darkroom control, in one workspace.

f01.title: Density inversion
f01.body: Start from the film’s density, sample the base, and use DCMY to rebuild the negative’s color and tone.

f02.title: Automatic RAW
f02.body: Import and go. Detect the frame, straighten, invert, and balance color, and let the roll’s repetitive work run itself.

f03.title: FFF auto crop
f03.body: Find frames in a strip scan and make a crop for each one. A strip comes in. Frames come out, each one editable.

f04.title: Many formats
f04.body: Bring camera RAW, DNG, TIFF, and FFF scans into the same darkroom, whatever the camera or scanner.

f05.title: Sprockets and borders
f05.body: Keep edge codes, fill sprocket holes white, and use the LIVE border template. The film edge can stay part of the picture.

f06.title: HDR output
f06.body: From the develop preview to Ultra HDR, so bright sources and fine tone hold up on screens that support it.

f07.title: Full color control
f07.body: DCMY, split white balance, curves, a mixer, color grading, LUTs, and local masks. From a faithful print to a personal look.

f08.title: Controls on the image
f08.body: Hold a key for the dial, drag a waveform, and keep moving with shortcuts. Strip crops keep a whole roll in one rhythm.

f09.title: Tethered capture
f09.body: Connect a supported camera for live view, remote release, and ingest. Or watch a folder and continue with the copy setup you already use.

f10.title: On-device dust removal
f10.body: Detect dust on this computer, edit the detected area, then repair it. Automatic detection and a manual brush, without inventing detail.

f11.title: LIVE motion
f11.body: Turn a still frame into a short motion piece. macOS can save a Live Photo. Windows can export a Live video.

f12.title: Works with agents
f12.body: Connect a supported agent through local MCP. Ask it to invert, crop, and grade, and take the file back for hand editing whenever you want.

workflows.eyebrow: 02 / Start from the film you have
workflows.body: Pick a path from the film type.

r1.title: Single RAW copies
r1.body: Turn on automatic processing, choose whether to keep or remove the film base, then check crop and color after import.

r2.title: Strip scans
r2.body: Choose the format, then split automatically or crop the strip by hand. Use absolute masks when each frame needs its own local adjustment.

r3.title: Slides and black-and-white
r3.body: Slides use the original-image path. Black-and-white negatives are inverted, then graded in gray and tone as needed.

auto.body: Turn on Auto Process. NextFrame detects the frame, crops, straightens, and inverts from your preset, then fills sprockets and handles color the way you set it.

s1.title: Choose the default
s1.body: Keep the film base or remove it, set in advance for the job.

s2.title: Import the RAW batch
s2.body: Wait for automatic processing, then review the result in Develop.

s3.title: Check, then export
s3.body: Hold A to run automatic processing again. Hold D to change the crop. Hold S to choose a tone mode.

strip.body: FFF auto split, strip crops, synced settings, and independent masks cover the path from scan to file. Share a look across the roll, and set exposure and color per frame.
